__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Application Prometheus
__inputs.description: Choose the Prometheus data source that scrapes the BFF /metrics listener and contains dial_chat_generations_active with otel_scope_name="dial-chat-api". An OTLP data source may use different metric names or labels.

title: DIAL BFF - Overview / HTTP
description: Select one environment/namespace and one scrape job to avoid mixing environments or double scraping. Missing cluster labels are supported by Cluster=All. No samples is not a health signal. Raw-server lifecycle metrics include tested guard/parser rejections and unmatched requests; the listener follows Express's registered request listener, so timing is not guaranteed to start before all synchronous processing. Arrival/in-flight ignore Route and include static/OPTIONS traffic; exact /api/health and /metrics URLs are excluded. Backend streaming classification uses four fixed /api/v1 routes; custom prefixes need care. Scrape health requires its own configured job. Trace links search the selected service/time range only, not a route, pod, or exact request.

list.name: trace_service
list.label: Trace service.name
list.description: Actual OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, independent of metric scope. Literal service name; quotes/backslashes require custom Explore JSON escaping.

list.name: scrape_job
list.label: Scrape health job
list.description: Exact Prometheus scrape job for this BFF, as it appears on the up series rather than on the application metrics. The default dial-chat-metrics matches the reference deployment; other deployments relabel the job, and Prometheus Operator targets carry names such as <namespace>/<service-monitor>. Confirm the value with group by (job, pod, instance) (up{namespace="<namespace>"}). Required for the up panel; avoids showing unrelated targets when the metric Job selector is All.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard

options.content: **HTTP transport.** Choose one workload and scrape job. Route does not filter arrivals or in-flight requests.

panels.title: Arrivals in period (est.)
panels.description: Estimated count over the full selected period. Increase is calculated per source series before aggregation; rounding affects display only. Missing series remain missing. Route filter does not apply.

panels.title: In flight at range end
panels.description: Instant observation at the selected range end, summed across the selected processes. Missing series remain missing. Route filter does not apply.

targets.expr: sum(sum by (cluster, namespace, job, pod, instance) (dial_chat_http_requests_active{otel_scope_name="dial-chat-api",cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",job=~"$job",pod=~"$pod",http_request_method=~"$http_method"}))

panels.title: Ended requests in period (est.)
panels.description: Estimated count over the full selected period. Increase is calculated per source series before aggregation; rounding affects display only. Missing series remain missing. Includes completed, aborted, and error outcomes; route filter applies.

panels.title: Traffic — arrivals and in-flight ignore Route
Request arrivals / second
panels.description: Arrivals observed by the raw request listener, including static/OPTIONS and tested guard/parser rejections. Excludes exact /api/health and /metrics. No route label at entry; Method applies, Route does not. These are BFF observations, not ingress arrivals.

panels.title: In-flight requests by process
panels.description: Outstanding observed HTTP transport lifecycles, not backend generations. Method applies, Route does not. No zero fallback: missing telemetry stays missing; a method series may be absent until its first request.

targets.expr: sum by (cluster, namespace, job, pod, instance) (dial_chat_http_requests_active{otel_scope_name="dial-chat-api",cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",job=~"$job",pod=~"$pod",http_request_method=~"$http_method"})

panels.title: Completed responses / second by status
panels.description: Only requests whose transport outcome was completed (a status line was sent and finish fired). Aborted/error outcomes are shown separately below, not folded in here.

panels.title: 4xx and 5xx share of completed responses
panels.description: Both numerator and denominator are restricted to dial.chat.http.outcome="completed" — this is the fraction of responses the BFF actually completed that were 4xx/5xx, not a fraction of all arrived requests. Aborted/error outcomes never enter this denominator; see the panel below for those. The percentage axis scales automatically from zero to show small changes.

panels.title: Aborted and failed transports / second
panels.description: aborted_before_response, aborted_during_response, and error are separate from HTTP status fractions. These categories do not prove which peer caused the transport to close. Status is absent if headers were never sent.

panels.title: Successful ordinary responses — latency
panels.description: Completed 2xx ordinary responses only. Errors are separate. Ordinary includes synchronous generation/files and may include SSE under a custom API_PREFIX because backend classification is fixed. Quantiles aggregate buckets and are hidden when the quantile falls above the last finite 60s bucket; mean remains available.

links.title: Search service traces in this time range (not an exact request)

panels.title: 4xx and 5xx ordinary responses — mean latency
panels.description: Mean of completed ordinary error responses, separate from successful response latency. No matching traffic gives no mean; this is not a request error rate.

panels.title: Streaming transports — mean duration
panels.description: Terminal transport duration for the four exact /api/v1 SSE routes, split by outcome. Includes interrupted streams, not just completed ones; still-running streams have no duration sample. Mean supports durations above 60s. This is not backend generation lifetime.

links.title: Search service traces in this time range (not an exact request)

panels.title: Streaming transports ending after 60s — share
panels.description: Fraction beyond the largest finite bucket, by route/outcome. Streaming p95 is omitted because a tail in +Inf cannot be located precisely. No terminal observations means no value. The percentage axis scales automatically from zero to show small changes.

panels.title: Route comparisons — snapshot at range end
Busiest endpoints — recent rate
panels.description: Terminal completed-response rate, not per-route arrival RPS. Snapshot at the selected range end, using $__rate_interval. At most ten rows; this is not a ranking by period totals.

value.title: Search service traces in this time range (not an exact request)

panels.title: Slowest routes — recent p95
panels.description: Completed 2xx ordinary responses. Buckets aggregated by route; unavailable quantiles beyond the 60s finite bound are omitted. Ordinary is the backend classification, not a guarantee of a short REST operation. Snapshot at the selected range end, using $__rate_interval. At most ten rows; this is not a ranking by period totals.

value.title: Search service traces in this time range (not an exact request)

targets.expr: topk(10, (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_route) (rate(dial_chat_http_response_duration_bucket{otel_scope_name="dial-chat-api",cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",job=~"$job",pod=~"$pod",http_route=~"$http_route",http_request_method=~"$http_method",dial_chat_http_transport_kind="ordinary",dial_chat_http_outcome="completed",http_response_status_code=~"2.."}[$__rate_interval])))) and ((sum by (http_route)(rate(dial_chat_http_response_duration_bucket{otel_scope_name="dial-chat-api",cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",job=~"$job",pod=~"$pod",http_route=~"$http_route",http_request_method=~"$http_method",dial_chat_http_transport_kind="ordinary",dial_chat_http_outcome="completed",http_response_status_code=~"2..",le=~"60([.]0+)?"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by (http_route)(rate(dial_chat_http_response_duration_count{otel_scope_name="dial-chat-api",cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",job=~"$job",pod=~"$pod",http_route=~"$http_route",http_request_method=~"$http_method",dial_chat_http_transport_kind="ordinary",dial_chat_http_outcome="completed",http_response_status_code=~"2.."}[$__rate_interval])) > 0) >= 0.95))

panels.title: Routes returning 4xx or 5xx — recent rate
panels.description: Completed 4xx/5xx responses by route/status; successful redirects are excluded. Unmatched parser/404 outcomes may share the unmatched route label. Snapshot at the selected range end, using $__rate_interval. At most ten rows; this is not a ranking by period totals.

value.title: Search service traces in this time range (not an exact request)

panels.title: Collection health — uses the Scrape health job
Scrape target status over time
panels.description: Configure the separate Scrape-health job variable with the exact BFF job, taken from the up series and not from the metric Job selector; the two names differ in most deployments. This panel ignores Route/Method and the metric Job selector. No matching up series means unknown/not configured, not healthy. Value 1 means scrape success only, not application or ingress availability. On Grafana versions using legacy interpolation, job names containing quotes need verified custom string escaping.

options.content: Select a Tempo datasource and set **Trace service.name** to the deployed OTEL_SERVICE_NAME (default @epam/chat-api). Data links search that service in the current time range; they do not apply route/pod/cluster filters or identify an exact request. The current app does not establish http.route on server spans. Verify attributes before adding route filtering. Loki navigation and exemplars are not configured. Service-name values containing quotes/backslashes need a custom escaped Explore link.
